title: Chinese Cucumber Salad
description: Chinese Cucumber Salad is a refreshing Sichuan-style cold dish made with smashed cucumbers tossed in a bright, aromatic dressing of fresh garlic, light soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and chili oil. The smashed cucumber technique creates a rustic texture with plenty of cracks for the savory, tangy, and spicy dressing to cling to.

ingredients.title: For the Dressing
items: Chinese black vinegar – 1 tsp (or rice vinegar)
Chili oil – ½ tsp, adjusted to taste

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Cucumbers
steps: Place each cucumber on a cutting board and gently smash it with the flat side of a knife or a rolling pin to create cracks along the flesh.
Cut the smashed cucumbers into bite-sized pieces.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Salting the Cucumbers
steps: Place the cucumber pieces in a bowl and sprinkle evenly with salt.
Let them sit for 10–15 minutes to draw out excess water.
Drain the released liquid and gently pat the cucumbers dry with paper towels.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Preparing the Dressing
steps: In a small bowl, combine minced garlic, light soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and chili oil.
Mix thoroughly until the sugar dissolves and the dressing is well balanced.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Assembling the Salad
steps: Add the prepared cucumbers to the dressing.
Toss gently but thoroughly until the dressing coats all the cucumber pieces.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the salad and add chopped cilantro or scallions if desired.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Chilling & Serving
steps: Refrigerate the dressed cucumber salad for 15–20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve cold on a chilled shallow plate.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve chilled as a refreshing appetizer or cold side dish.
Pair with fried rice, noodles, dumplings, or spicy Chinese dishes.
Serve on a chilled shallow plate and garnish immediately before serving for a professional presentation.

chefTips: Smashing the cucumbers instead of thinly slicing them creates a rustic texture and provides more surface area for the dressing to cling to.
Taste the dressing before combining and adjust the sweetness, saltiness, acidity, and heat for a balanced flavor.
Use freshly minced garlic for the brightest and most aromatic result.
Drizzle chili oil lightly for a more controlled level of heat and an attractive presentation.
Salting the cucumbers before dressing helps remove excess water and prevents the finished salad from becoming watery.
Keep the salad chilled and add the final sesame seeds and fresh herbs just before serving.
